subject.title: [Bug]: Trajectory files fed back as context cause unbounded token consumption and unexpected API billing

question: Is current source-level trajectory/session filtering sufficient to close this billing report, or should it stay open until a live Windows or packaged `openclaw chat --session <fresh-key>` proof confirms no trajectory bytes reach provider input?
rationale: The source guardrails look relevant, but the user-visible harm is provider billing, and the exact current-main runtime path has not been proven after those guardrails.

options.title: Require current-main proof
options.body: Keep this issue open until a focused packaged or Windows fresh-session run shows large trajectory sidecars do not affect provider input tokens.

options.title: Close as source-covered
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept the existing classifier, TUI, gateway, and reseed guards as sufficient proof for the billing path.

options.title: Patch after failed proof
options.body: If the focused proof still shows trajectory-derived context, queue a narrow fix for the specific ingestion path found by that run.

recommendation.title: Require current-main proof
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a focused packaged or Windows fresh-session run shows large trajectory sidecars do not affect provider input tokens.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the central trajectory artifact boundary is the trajectory sidecar cleanup work, and this choice is about proof sufficiency for that boundary.
